newsitem.title: INDIA: India 1996/97 coal output to fall short of demand.
newsitem.headline: India 1996/97 coal output to fall short of demand.

text.p: India's domestic production of coal will fall short of demand in 1996/97 (April-March), the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE) said.
"The (coal) demand for the year 1996/97 from various coal consuming sectors has shown a sharp and unanticipated increase," the independent Bombay-based think-tank said in a report.
It said the demand from power sector alone was 210 millon tonnes of coal in 1996/97 as against 185.30 million tonnes indicated for the year.

"On the other hand, as a result of various constraints, including those of finances, land acquisition and transportation, coal companies have indicated a domestic production of only 288.65 million tonnes for 1996/97," CMIE said.
This represents a 6.8 percent rise over the actual production of 270.13 million tonnes in 1995/96.

"As a result of this, the planning commission has estimated that the gap between demand and availability ofraw coal from domestic sources during the year 1996/97 would be 34.35 million tonnes," the CMIE report said.
